summary:
Submitted a check product that escalates the active consequence candidate to an obligation and runs it end to end.

Context from the index: two findings are confirmed_in_scope (oblig-config-from-durable-entry and oblig-config-readout-index), the heartbeat candidate is explained, candidate 1dc85f22… is the active concrete_suspicion on the excluded consequence of the first finding, map v5 is the accepted basis, and capacity still holds 2 audit units, 4 semantic reviews and 6 experiments.

Product contents (draft-relative submission.json with plan_phantom_commit.json and harness_phantom_commit.go):

New obligation oblig-config-committed-backed-by-entry (consensus_safety): a server must not treat a configuration as committed unless the log entry at that configuration index is a configuration entry encoding that configuration. It is bound to Raft.leaderLoop (SR-LEADER-LOOP, 667-963), the leader commit path that promotes configurations.latest to committed once its index falls within the commit index without inspecting the entry stored there; the question is the active candidate's, updated only in disposition (ready_for_check) so it stays on its accepted basis.

The check drives the full consequence path: node A bootstraps as a single voter and commits its no-op; one injected StoreLogs failure during AddVoter leaves A holding a latest configuration whose entry was never written; node B joins unbootstrapped with an empty configuration over connected in-memory transports; A then campaigns under the adopted voter set, wins with B's vote, commits an entry of its own term, and the harness admits the phantom_config_adopted event and reports committed_config_state with the committed voter count and index, the type of the log entry stored at that index, the read error and the peer's voter count. The property is an implication: when the committed configuration contains the adopted voter set, the entry at that configuration index must be a configuration entry — so a commit of a configuration that no log entry encodes is a violation.

Preflight `validate` returned valid=true with no diagnostics. Acceptance, clean-copy execution and the observed result remain with the controller; a checker-correspondence review would be the next step if another turn is available.
